front.title: Linking an Agent's DNS Name to its OAuth Client

abstract.t:
Software agents increasingly call agents and services operated by other organizations. A receiving organization often wants to know two things about any such caller: that it is the agent it claims to be, and that the organization operating it still authorizes it. Existing approaches to the second question require a trust relationship between the two organizations' authorization servers.
This document defines a DNS record by which the owner of a domain links an agent's DNS name to the OAuth client that the agent uses at the owner's own authorization server. The sending agent presents a fresh access token for that client; the receiver verifies the token against the record and against the issuer's published keys. No trust relationship, registration or federation between the two organizations is needed, and disabling the client at the sending organization's authorization server stops the agent being accepted by every receiver.
